rows.grounds: The class is global, unscoped and in `@layer components` at all three datums, so it applies to any element that carries it, wherever it mounts. Custom properties, and the `@container style(--glass-backdrop: light)` arms that read one, resolve through DOM ancestors. rows.cureShape: ANSWER: yes for the class, no for ancestor tokens. `.glass-floating` is an unscoped class rule in @layer components (ladder.css), so any element carrying it paints the floating tier, teleported or not. glass-ui's portalled roots carry it on the portalled element: Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu and its sub-content through overlayContentAttrs, plus Dialog and Sheet. What does not cross the portal is inheritance: `--glass-*`, `--radius-ctx` or `--glass-backdrop` (which drives the `@container style(--glass-backdrop: light)` arms) set on an in-tree wrapper never reach content teleported to body. Set those on :root, on the portalled root through its class prop, or on the portal target. The `.dark` arm reaches portalled content because `.dark` sits on html.
rows.replyLine: O-32 §4.3 (glass-floating and portals): yes for the class, no for ancestor tokens, and the answer is the same at 8.0.0, 9.0.0 and HEAD. `.glass-floating` is an unscoped class rule in @layer components, so it paints any element that carries it, teleported or not, and our portalled roots (Tooltip, Popover, DropdownMenu, Dialog, Sheet) carry it on the portalled element.
